findings.claim: Bumping the hardcoded cache `version` invalidates every existing on-disk module cache; unless pruning exists elsewhere, the previous version's cache directory/files are orphaned rather than removed, leaking disk space on each bump.
findings.rationale: The version string appears to participate in the cache key/path (the class tracks rootCache, metadataFilePath and fsCacheRoots). Changing it makes prior entries unreachable. The pruning logic is not visible in this hunk, so I am only moderately confident — if the class already deletes cache roots whose version differs, this is a non-issue. Worth confirming a cleanup path for stale versions exists.

findings.claim: The cache version is a manually maintained literal, so any change to cached-module serialization or semantics that lands without a matching bump will silently serve stale cached output.
findings.rationale: Inherent fragility of the pattern rather than a defect introduced here; flagged only because this change is exactly a manual bump, meaning correctness depends on developers remembering. Low confidence that action is needed in this PR — mainly worth verifying the bump corresponds to a real semantics change in the same change set.
